title: Connectivity-admissible repair history is not a new persistent-credit primitive
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that EvoDRC's connectivity-gated repair history defines a novel credit semantics for persistent skill evolution because accepted repair records can coexist with locally harmful DRC outcomes.

counter_explanation.statement: EvoDRC's released logs show a real label mismatch, but the mismatch is already explained by the distinction between feasibility/admissibility and causal utility credit. Across 24 released units with both an independent local DRC score and a gate verdict, all 24 pass the connectivity gate while 10/24 are locally net worse; seven of those locally harmful units occur in globally improving iterations. The gate therefore cannot identify positive local utility. Existing causal-utility admission principles already require persistent artifacts to be credited from matched downstream effect rather than feasibility, acceptance, or shared aggregate success.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: If gated_in is only an admissibility predicate, then connectivity-preserved repairs may have positive, zero, or negative local DRC utility, and a globally improving iteration can contain locally harmful accepted actions. A same-information utility/effect credit baseline would distinguish those cases using local or matched causal outcome polarity without introducing a new EvoDRC-specific credit primitive.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Feasibility or admissibility is not causal credit. Persistent self-evolution should assign positive credit only from a utility/effect label at the causal unit whose behavior is being persisted, or from a same-information estimator of that local effect.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Search only for a persistent-skill failure that remains after local causal utility/effect polarity is explicitly available and matched at the repair unit: for example, two records with the same local causal utility and admissibility but different later persistent-skill consequences that a same-information causal-utility baseline cannot express.
counter_explanation.scope: EvoDRC released unit-gate repair histories and persistent skill evolution at first-party commit 0a9b4c732cadce7a0718467aa10ef8a741da369a.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: Wrong-layer bookkeeping alone: each repair record is copied to all touched-layer histories in the released implementation.
All admitted repairs have positive local effect: 10/24 independently scored gated-in units have positive drc_delta, i.e. locally worse DRC utility.
Only globally bad iterations create the mismatch: seven locally harmful gated-in units occur while the corresponding whole-block iteration improves.

Skill evolution is globally harmful: first-party Ablation 2 (fixed skills) is generally worse than full EvoDRC, including Block7 final 358 versus 275, so the audit does not support that broader claim.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only on a preregistered unit-matched substrate where feasibility/admissibility, local causal utility polarity, and the persisted semantic record are all independently observed; require a later persistent-skill harm/benefit residual among units matched on local causal utility and admissibility that survives a same-information causal-utility/difference-reward baseline.
